advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the attach-time local-resolvability requirement with the close-check's tolerance of locally-absent attached SHAs (document why they differ, or align them).
evidence: _lib_writes.py:720-725: `unresolvable = commit_impact.unresolvable_shas(...)` then raises 'did not resolve to a commit in this repository; nothing was recorded'
close_precheck.py:276: `continue  # an attached SHA absent from this clone is not evidence of a problem`
commit_impact.py comment: 'an attached SHA may legitimately live in another clone (or simply be unfetched)'
advisory.finding: The attach seam rejects any SHA that does not resolve to a commit in the LOCAL repo (commit_impact.unresolvable_shas), but the close check (_check_file_impact_vs_diff) deliberately tolerates an attached SHA being absent from the local clone ('may legitimately live in another clone, or simply be unfetched') and silently skips it. Because attach-time validation forbids attaching a locally-unresolvable SHA in the first place, the 'foreign clone' skip branch can only be reached if the repo state changed AFTER attach (re-clone / shallow fetch / gc). The two seams thus encode contradictory assumptions about SHA locality; the skip branch's stated justification does not hold at attach time.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Dedup the union of attached + referencing SHAs before the per-commit git probes in _check_file_impact_vs_diff.
evidence: close_precheck.py:264: `for sha in _attached_commit_shas(accepted_ids, tracker) + list(referencing):`
No set/dedup is applied; a commit both attached and referencing runs the full git probe pair twice.
advisory.finding: In _check_file_impact_vs_diff, a SHA that appears in BOTH the attached-commits list and the referencing scan is processed twice (`_attached_commit_shas(...) + list(referencing)` with no dedup), incurring duplicate git subprocess calls (is_merge_commit, changed_paths) per commit. Harmless for correctness but wasteful on large ticket subtrees.

Semantic inconsistency: close_precheck._check_file_impact_vs_diff treats an attached SHA absent from this clone as 'not evidence of a problem' (skipped), yet attach-time validation now hard-rejects that same foreign SHA
advisory.finding: The pre-existing public library seam `rebar.attach_commits` now validates every SHA against the local git repo (`commit_impact.unresolvable_shas`) and raises `RebarError` for any SHA that does not resolve to a commit object. This narrows a previously-valid input: callers that attach arbitrary/foreign SHA strings — which the seam accepted before — now break. Existing consumers pass fabricated SHAs that will no longer resolve.
scenarios: Any existing caller of rebar.attach_commits that records a SHA from another clone / not fetched locally
